items.title: 68356_Howard R. Scott oral history interview
items.q: Dr. Thompson was the doctor that brought me here.

ctx.x: Richmond, Virginia. And he was here when he was 20 years old, in 1888, he came to New York. And that blizzard so high, they didn't have the modern implements to clear a way, and it just stayed there til it melted. That's the way it was, then.

But he couldn't get any jobs outside of porters or janitor or what you call blue collar jobs. And -- but he loved horses, crazy about horses. He got a job with a white doctor, Dr. Thompson. And he drove for him, because in those days, doctors used to visit their patients. Of course, nowadays, you have to go to the doctor yourself. Doctors are scared to come out, they get mugged for dope, if they think they got dope.
